device_note: Locked to cpu, matching every existing checkpoint in this repo (MPS is available on this machine but was not used, to keep this run comparable to the pre-existing SI baseline checkpoints and to avoid an unstated protocol change).
pre_registered_expectation: Female digit accuracy under male-only training will stay near the female accuracy of the normally (sex-mixed) trained model on the SAME female speakers -- no significant, seed-stable drop. Behavioral corroboration of 'sex not load-bearing', consistent with the representational readout-sensitivity result (results/sex_direction/readout_sensitivity_run_meta.json). Written before any run in this script looked at a result.
decision_rule: Per architecture: average each of the 12 female speakers' accuracy across seeds 42/43/44 for both male-only-trained and SI-baseline models; bootstrap the PAIRED per-speaker difference over speakers. CI includes 0 (& seeds agree/non-significant) -> CORROBORATED. CI excludes 0 on the negative side & all 3 seeds negative -> TENSION_FLAG (flagged loudly, not smoothed over). Anything else (CI excludes 0 but seeds disagree in sign, or genuinely wide) -> UNDERPOWERED_DIRECTIONAL_ONLY (honest non-result).

excluded_by_design.train_female_test_male: NOT RUN. <=12 female training speakers makes any accuracy drop a sample-size confound, not a sex effect -- excluded per pre-registration.
excluded_by_design.balanced_50_50_dataset: NOT BUILT. 12 female speakers cap any balanced design; rebuilding an elaborate design on an unfixable sample was excluded per pre-registration.

n_flag: female test speakers n=12 (of 60 total; <=12 dataset-wide) -- directional, not a population claim
confound_note: The SI-baseline model (condition C) was itself TRAINED on 7 of the 12 female test speakers and used 2 more for early-stop selection (val) -- only 3 (the SI regime's own test fold) are genuinely held out from it. See female_speaker_si_roles below. A full-12 comparison therefore mixes true cross-sex generalization with plain speaker memorization for condition C only (condition A trained on zero female speakers, so it has no such advantage) -- this can by itself produce an apparent female-accuracy 'drop' under male-only training that has nothing to do with sex. Two verdicts are reported per architecture: 'verdict_all_12' (confounded, n=12) and 'verdict_held_out_only' (clean but underpowered, n=3, the SI regime's own 3-speaker test fold) -- the held-out-only verdict is the one that actually speaks to cross-sex generalization; the all-12 verdict is reported for transparency, not as the headline.
